title: Young Miles Davis sits in for Buddy Anderson
summary: A high-school trumpeter hanging around the dance hall fills in when Anderson falls ill, until Marion Hazle arrives.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Anyway, we're playing in... No. Before we went in the Plantation, we had three days in..> It was a dance hall there, that's what it was. We had three days in a dance hall. And this kid used to come around and stand in front of the band with his trumpet, like most young guys do when they play the instrument. They come around where the more mature musicians are, or the pros or whatever, the traveling bands, and they stand around for one reason or another. Most times they like to let you know that they play an instrument, and that way they get to know you better.
So anyway, this kid was around for a couple of nights,

and he'd begun to talk to Dizzy and me, he talked to members of the band. I think it was about the third night that we were there, this trumpet player, Buddy Anderson, got sick, and they had to rush him to the hospital. They found out that he had some lung trouble, I think, which was the result of him actually losing that lung. But he's still around, and I understand, very healthy. The last time I saw him was back in the Sixties in Oklahoma City.

But we worked without a trumpet player that night. So this kid was there, and Dizzy asked him if he could read, you know. I guess it was like any young high school musician who knew some (?), and then he was saying, "Yeah, I can read." Anyway, Dizzy had him come up and sit in the band and play this guy's part. And he did well, you know. What we learned, though, was that he'd just come out of high school. And this fellow's name was Miles Davis.

Miles sat in with the band until they sent for another trumpet player that I had known here in Washington, but he was also from Pittsburgh. His name was Marion Hazle; everybody called him Boonie. So Miles sat in and played... That was my first acquaintance with Miles Davis.
